name: Developmental Editing
title: Developmental Editing
answer: Developmental editing is the work of shaping a manuscript at the level of structure, argument, character and pacing rather than at the level of commas and typos. It sits upstream of copy editing and proofreading, and it is the stage where a book's spine is decided: what the throughline is, which chapters earn their place, where the reader is likely to lose the thread. In the literary arts it covers both fiction and nonfiction, from novels with a sagging middle act to memoirs that need a clearer chronology. The output is usually an editorial letter plus a marked-up manuscript, not a rewritten draft.

sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: The tools are ordinary ones: word processors, tracked changes, comment threads, and increasingly a shared document that author and editor can both annotate. Some editors now run a manuscript through a large language model to produce a chapter-by-chapter summary or a character list, which is faster than building one by hand and easier to check against the text. Others use outlining and mind-mapping software to test whether a proposed restructure holds together before the author commits to it. None of this replaces reading the whole book closely, which remains the core of the job.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: The work starts with a full read, often two, the first for the experience of the book and the second for its machinery. The editor then writes an editorial letter that names the two or three structural problems that matter most, explains why they matter, and suggests directions rather than dictating fixes. A second pass marks specific passages in the manuscript so the author can see the general note in situ. The author decides what to accept, and the editor's next job is to read the revision against the original letter and say whether the problem is actually solved.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: Confidentiality is the baseline: unpublished manuscripts are among the most sensitive documents a writer will ever hand to anyone, and nondisclosure terms are common. Credit and payment are usually set by contract, with developmental editing billed per project or per hour rather than as a share of royalties, and the editor's contribution is normally acknowledged in the book's front matter rather than on the cover. Where a model has been used to summarise or analyse a manuscript, that use is worth disclosing to the author, both because the text is unpublished and because the author may have views about it. The site tracks 92 active intellectual property lawsuits, a reminder that text and its provenance are live questions rather than settled ones.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: The likely direction is a split practice: routine structural diagnostics, summaries, continuity checks and outline testing increasingly handled by software, while the judgement calls about what a book is trying to be stay with a person who has read it closely. Editors who can articulate why a structure fails, and who can hold an author's confidence through a hard revision, will be the ones whose work is hardest to automate. Expect clearer norms about disclosing model use on unpublished manuscripts, and more pressure on contracts to say plainly what an editor did and what a tool did.
